witness_description: No witness. The full claim is not a self-contained finitely checkable proposition: it asserts that an unstated 'theorem' holds and hedges with 'typically allows for variations', neither of which has a decidable truth condition from the claim text alone.
refutation_explanation: The claim references 'the theorem' without stating it, so no graph can be tested against it; 'typically allows for variations ... in larger components or when interacting with other parts of the graph' is a non-quantified hedge naming no precise object or equivalence. The only precise, self-contained fragment in the claim (a single isolated directed 2-cycle has a reversal-invariant edge set, while reversing a k>=3 cycle yields a genuinely different edge set) was formalized and exhaustively checked with exact integer arithmetic over labelled directed k-cycles for k=2..12: the 2-cycle's edge set equals its reversal, and for every k in 3..12 the reversed edge set differs. That fragment admits no counterexample; the remainder of the claim supplies no data to refute.
search_space: Concrete fragment probe: canonical labelled directed k-cycles on vertices 0..k-1 with edges (i,(i+1) mod k), for every k in {2,...,12}; for each, exact frozenset comparison of the cycle's edge set with its reversal. Fixed deterministic iteration order, integers only, no floats, no randomness.
